source.label: thm:intro-algo
source.quote: For all \cBwK problems with $K$ actions, $d$ resources, time horizon $T$, and for all policy sets $\Pi$. Algorithm \CBalance achieves expected total reward $\Rew \geq \OPT(\Pi) - O\left( 1+\tfrac{1}{B}\,\OPT(\Pi)\right)\sqrt{dKT \; \log \left( dKT\,|\Pi| \right)}$, where $B = \min_i B_i$

results.notes: Regret = OPT(Pi) minus expected total reward; mapped to pseudo_regret. Paper's d is number of resources, renamed d_res. Algorithm not computationally efficient (paper explicitly gives no efficient implementation). Also holds w.r.t. LP benchmark OPT_LP.

source.label: thm:discretization
source.quote: Consider contextual dynamic pricing with a single product and prices in $[0,1]$. Use standard notation: supply $B$, policy set $\Pi$ and time horizon $T$. Assume Lipschitz demands with Lipschitz constant $L$. Then algorithm \CBalance with discretized policy set $\Pi_\eps$ ... achieves expected total reward $\Rew \geq \OPT(\Pi) - O( T^{3/5}\,B^{1/5}) \cdot \left(L \, \log \left(  T|\Pi| \right) \right)^{1/5}$

results.notes: Paper's L is the Lipschitz constant of the demand (sales rate), mapped to L_lip. For B = Omega(T) gives O(T^{4/5})(L log(T|Pi|))^{1/5}.
